title: Whether Dark Energy Evolves (DESI w0-wa Tension)
bottleneck: DESI DR1 and DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation data, combined with CMB and supernovae, prefer an evolving dark energy equation of state (w0 > -1, wa < 0) over a cosmological constant at 2.8-4.2 sigma depending on the supernova sample. It is unknown whether this is the first crack in LambdaCDM, a supernova systematics artifact, or a parameterization artifact of the w0-wa form. The statistical significance depends notably on which supernova compilation is used, ranging from 2.5 to nearly 4 sigma, which keeps systematics debates alive.
why_it_blocks: If dark energy evolves, the cosmological constant is dead and a dynamical field or modified gravity must replace it — the biggest shift in cosmology in 25 years.
current_state: DESI DR2 strengthens the hint but stays below discovery threshold; Euclid and Rubin Observatory data in the late 2020s should confirm or kill it. DESI's full five-year dataset plus Euclid's independent BAO measurements should push the question past the discovery threshold either way.
